econ-macro-01-c2.text: Dylan G. Rassier (2012). The Role of Profits and Income in the Statistical Discrepancy. Survey of Current Business, U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis.
econ-macro-01-c2.quote: The difference between GDP and GDI is known as the statistical discrepancy. Both GDP and GDI provide a complete picture of economic output, so the statistical discrepancy provides an indication of net measurement error.
econ-macro-01-c2.claim: In practice the three rarely match exactly, because measurement error creates a 'statistical discrepancy'.

econ-macro-01-c3.text: Jonathan D. Church (2016). Comparing the Consumer Price Index with the gross domestic product price index and gross domestic product implicit price deflator. Monthly Labor Review, U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.
econ-macro-01-c3.quote: but also measures price change for goods and services purchased by businesses, governments, and foreigners.
econ-macro-01-c3.claim: It's broader than CPI because it covers everything in GDP, while CPI covers only consumer goods.
